changes: Crooked scans are straightened: before a scanned page is read, a tilt of up to 10° is levelled out, and a page that's upside down or sideways is turned the right way up. Straight pages read better, so barcodes, zones, AI and field values all benefit, and the saved file is straight too. On by default; turn it off per profile on the Overview tab.

Each document keeps a record of its exports — where it went, when, and what it produced, such as the Therefore document number or the file written, or why it failed. It's shown under Exports in the review panel, and over the status in the Table view.
If one of a document's exports fails, retrying sends only the ones that failed, so the Therefore document isn't created twice. A failed export now says why in the status bar.

Exported documents stay Exported, including in Trash, and Export says why it skipped any: already exported (Mark ready to send again), not ready, or no export set up. When nothing was exported, a message says so.
Settings opens straight away instead of waiting while scanners are found; the scanner list fills in a moment later.
Two settings — sending page images to the AI, and showing a TWAIN scanner's own settings window — were lost when Capture restarted. They're now kept.
Therefore export reads amounts and dates the way the field validated them: with a currency symbol, thousands separators, and the document type's locale (e.g. day-first dates).
Adding pages to a redacted document now marks its redactions as needing to be applied again, instead of still showing it as redacted.
Exports and AI calls have longer to finish (5 minutes) for large scans and slower models; Test connection gives up after 20 seconds.

More reliable redaction service, a partial AI model download no longer left behind, an unexpected error is shown instead of closing Capture, and with blank-page removal on, scanned PDF pages are read from the right page.

Windows: TWAIN scanners. Production document scanners such as Canon imageFORMULA, Ricoh/Fujitsu fi, Kodak Alaris and Epson DS now appear in Settings ▸ Scanning once their TWAIN driver is installed, alongside WIA scanners — each labelled (TWAIN) or (WIA). Feeder, duplex, colour or greyscale and resolution are set from Capture; pages are counted as they arrive, and stopping a scan keeps the pages already scanned.
TWAIN scanners can show the manufacturer's own settings window before each scan, for options Capture doesn't set itself: tick Show the scanner's own settings before each scan in Settings ▸ Scanning.

TWAIN scanners give clear messages when the feeder is empty, the scanner's cover is open, a scan stops before the feeder is empty (a jam or two sheets fed together), or another program is using the scanner.
Settings no longer offers Flatbed for a scanner that only has a feeder when it's chosen automatically.

Windows: WIA scanners now appear in Capture — previously none were listed, so Scan had nothing to scan from. This includes scanners using the driver Windows installs itself, such as a Canon LiDE over USB, which now show their flatbed and resolutions, and their pages are saved compressed rather than as large uncompressed images.

Network scanners: scanners macOS lists in Printers & Scanners — AirScan and other network scanners — now appear in Capture, not just USB ones. If a scanner says it's busy, close Image Capture or any other app that has it open.
A pass through the scanner now stays together as one document, like a multi-page PDF, unless the profile's rules or AI separation split it. Previously each scanned page became its own document.
Capture always asks whether to keep scanning: more pages are added to the document, or, if the pass was split into several documents, more documents go into the same batch.
Long scans: the status bar counts pages as they arrive, the scanner can take as long as it needs for a large stack, and if it jams or you cancel, the pages already scanned are kept and imported.
The status bar shows progress while importing: reading each page, sending pages to the AI for separation, and saving each document. Test capture shows the same.

AI separation can be given extra rules for a profile's batches — Additional guidance for the AI on the profile's Overview, e.g. "a page titled TRANSMITTAL always starts a new document". Check changes with Test capture: on the local model, extra wording can make splitting worse.

AI document separation: a profile can have AI decide where documents start in a mixed stack. Choose Split documents only — each document's type then comes from its pages' identify rules, or the fallback type — or Split and classify documents, where the AI also chooses the type. Barcodes, separator sheets and first-page rules still apply, and splits the AI is unsure of go to Needs review with its reason.

Ready-made AI document types: + From catalog adds Invoice, Credit Note, Statement, Purchase Order, Remittance Advice, Delivery Docket, Receipt, Contract or Correspondence, with a description for the AI and the AI fields those documents usually carry. Your own types work too — give them an AI description. New AI fields cover credit notes, statements and remittances.

Test capture shows the pages in each document and the AI's reasons, names documents that fit none of the profile's types ("AI: Bank Statement") so you can see which types to add, and accepts files and folders dragged onto it.

Change a document's type in review: click the Type chip above the page and choose another type from its profile. Fields are extracted again for that type, keeping any values you typed into fields of the same name.

OCR with Azure AI Document Intelligence, for handwriting and poor scans: add an Azure Document Intelligence connection, then have a profile send every scanned page to Azure, or only pages the built-in OCR reads poorly.

AI extraction works with Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Foundry endpoints (resource, deployment or project address, with an api-key header) and with GPT-5 and other reasoning models. Settings ▸ AI extraction has a Test button that shows the service's answer, or its error and the address called.
TIFF files can be imported: every page of a multi-page TIFF, including Group 4 fax compression, at the resolution the scanner recorded.
Settings ▸ AI extraction can stop page images being sent for AI separation, for models that can't read images.

Choosing the category for an existing Therefore export now ticks only the fields the export already had, instead of every field. This makes repointing an export at another Therefore system much quicker: fields are matched by name there, because field numbers differ between systems.
Longer field messages in review, such as "AI isn't set up", now show under the field instead of over its name.

AI fields now say why they're empty. If AI isn't set up, each AI field shows "AI isn't set up" and the document goes to review. If the AI service fails, its fields show the error — including the service's own message, such as an incorrect API key — and the rest of the document is still indexed instead of the whole capture failing.

The AI field catalog has two new Invoice types: ABN (the supplier's Australian Business Number, in NN NNN NNN NNN format) and Total Net (the invoice total before tax). New built-in types are now added to an existing catalog file once, so they appear without resetting it; types you've deleted or edited are left alone.
A Therefore export's field mapping can now be cleared with the ✕ beside it, leaving that Therefore field unmapped.

Settings ▸ Connections replaces the Therefore tab. Add as many Therefore servers and REST services as you need, each with its own name and sign-in, and test each one. Your existing Therefore setup moves across automatically as a connection called "Therefore".

Each Therefore export chooses which connection it uses. Re-picking a category on a different server matches fields by name rather than number, so a profile imported from another system can be repointed without remapping fields.

Scripts can call a connection by name — for example Connections["Therefore"].PostAsync("ExecuteSingleQuery", …) — with requests signed using its stored credentials, which the script never sees. A connection only sends requests to its own server.
Button field scripts can show a message with await Message("…") and ask a question with await Confirm("…"). Time spent reading a dialog doesn't count toward the button's timeout.
Help ▸ scripting has new examples, including looking up a Therefore category by name and then searching it for a document.
A newly added field now opens on its General tab.
Fields can have a description, set on the field's General tab in the profile designer. While indexing, it shows as an ⓘ tip beside the field and on its Table column header.

Script fields, and Text or Lookup fields with a template, now update as soon as a field they use is changed in review — for example a Department script that follows a Document Kind dropdown. Values typed in by hand are left alone.

Settings ▸ Back up… saves your choice of settings, capture profiles (with their sample files), custom redaction sets and the AI field catalog to one .zip, and Restore… puts back whichever parts you pick — handy for a new computer or moving to the Microsoft Store version. These replace Import/Export settings; Restore still accepts settings files saved by Export settings.

Conditional fields: a field's new Conditional tab sets when it's used — for example when Document Kind is Invoice or Credit Note. Rules can test several values, a Yes/No answer, or whether a field is filled in, and can be combined with all/any. While its rules don't match, the field is disabled or hidden, isn't required, and isn't exported.
An arrow on the divider next to the Indexes panel, and next to the profile designer's settings panel, widens that panel to double its width; click it again to restore it.
Yes/No fields with a default such as 1 now show as Yes or No in Table mode.
Capture is now packaged for the Microsoft Store. The Store version installs and updates through the Store, so it doesn't check GitHub for updates.
Added a privacy policy.

New "Capture separator sheet" rule for batches and documents — print a ready-made Document or Batch separator sheet from More ▸ Separator sheets and use it to split scans without designing or configuring a barcode.
Yes/No index fields (Boolean format) now edit as a checkbox in the review panel and Table mode. A blank value stays unanswered, so a mandatory Yes/No field is still flagged until someone answers it.
Yes/No values are read the same way everywhere (yes/no, true/false, 1/0), including when exporting to a Therefore logical field.
About now includes this version history.
Re-picking a Therefore category with a different number keeps field mappings by matching field names — useful after importing a configuration from another Therefore system.
A Therefore export no longer reports failure when a workflow moves the new document to another category straight after it's saved.
Fixed Statistics tooltips and Table/Preview column widths.
An import failure that was previously silent is now logged.
Edit index fields directly in Table mode, moving between cells with Tab and Shift+Tab.
Displayed batch numbers restart each session.
Manual batches show status indicators instead of status text.
A first-run setup wizard helps configure Capture the first time it starts.
Fixed document status when no capture profile is applied.
Aligned the Statistics chart.
Remove blank pages automatically on ingestion.
Rotate pages from the page strip.
New REST export, and PDF/A output.
Fixed the capture profile picker.
New Statistics window.
Records when each document was last exported.
Undo for page delete, split and reorder.
Drag to reorder rules and exports, and copy an export to another document type.
Batch-aware scanning and importing, and Trash management.
Drag pages to reorder them, including to the last position.
Drag to reorder document types; removing one now asks for confirmation.
A None entry in the capture profile picker.
Hidden index fields are grouped at the bottom of the field list.
Fixed oversized pages from scanned or imported documents, and a crash with single-page scans or non-PDF imports.
Removed the Therefore export's Fixed/Constant value mapping option.
Updated in-app Help, with more detail on scripting.
Fixed scripting in the packaged macOS app.
Script errors now show the underlying cause instead of a generic initialisation failure.
Empty fields are left out of Therefore exports so Therefore's own field defaults apply.
Grab field values straight from the document image in Preview mode.
"Apply profile" reclassifies selected documents under another capture profile.
"Export selected to PDF" for ad hoc exports.
Scan or import with no capture profile selected (Unsorted).
AI-extracted values are located and highlighted on the page where possible.
Table view fixes for selection, scrolling and column widths.
The field editor is split into General, Extraction and Scripting tabs, and the field list can be resized.
Fixed Therefore export failing with a date/time error.
Fixed input field text alignment and control heights.
Faster processing: OCR runs in parallel and reloads do less work.
Capture configuration rebuilt around unified Capture Profiles.
Search added to in-app Help, plus app-wide UI fixes.
